content.latin: Romæ sancti Lini, Papæ et Mártyris, qui, primus post beátum Petrum Apóstolum, Romanam Ecclésiam gubernávit, et, martýrio coronátus, sepúltus est in Vaticáno, prope eúndem Apóstolum.
content.english: At Rome, the holy martyr Pope Linus. He was the first successor of the blessed Apostle Peter in the government of the Church of Rome, was crowned with martyrdom, and is buried upon the Vatican Hill, hard by the Apostle.

content.latin: Icónii, in Lycaónia, sanctæ Theclæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, a sancto Paulo Apóstolo ad fidem perdúcta, ignes ac béstias, sub Neróne Imperatóre, in Christi confessióne devícit; et, post plúrima ad multórum doctrínam superáta certámina, venit Seleucíam, ibíque requiévit in pace. Ipsam vero sancti Patres summis láudibus celebrárunt.
content.english: At Iconium, in Lycaonia, the holy Virgin and martyr Thecla. She was converted to the faith by the holy Apostle Paul. Under the Emperor Nero she overcame fire and beasts for her confession of Christ, and after many contendings, wherein she was victorious, for the teaching of many, she came to Seleucia, and there fell asleep in peace. The holy Fathers do greatly extol her.

content.latin: In Hispánia sanctárum mulíerum Xantíppæ et Polýxenæ, quæ fuérunt Apostolórum discípulæ.
content.english: In Campania is made commemoration of the blessed Sosius, Deacon of the Church of Miseno. One while when he was reading the Gospel in the church, the holy Bishop Januarius saw flames rising from his head, and foretold that he would be a martyr. Neither was it many days afterward, when, being himself of the age of thirty years, he was beheaded along with the said Bishop, and so received martyrdom.

content.english: At Ancona, holy Constantius, watchman of the Church [of St. Stephen,] who was remarkable for his grace of working miracles.

content.latin: 39:2 Exspéctans exspectávi Dóminum, * et inténdit mihi.
content.english: 39:2 With expectation I have waited for the Lord, * and he was attentive to me.

segments.t: Exspéctans exspectávi Dóminum, * et inténdit mihi.

content.latin: 39:3 Et exaudívit preces meas: * et edúxit me de lacu misériæ, et de luto fæcis.
content.english: 39:3 And he heard my prayers, * and brought me out of the pit of misery and the mire of dregs.

segments.t: Et exaudívit preces meas: * et edúxit me de lacu misériæ, et de luto fæcis.

content.latin: 39:3 Et státuit super petram pedes meos: * et diréxit gressus meos.
content.english: 39:3 And he set my feet upon a rock, * and directed my steps.

segments.t: Et státuit super petram pedes meos: * et diréxit gressus meos.

content.latin: 39:4 Et immísit in os meum cánticum novum, * carmen Deo nostro.
content.english: 39:4 And he put a new canticle into my mouth, * a song to our God.

segments.t: Et immísit in os meum cánticum novum, * carmen Deo nostro.

content.latin: 39:4 Vidébunt multi, et timébunt: * et sperábunt in Dómino.
content.english: 39:4 Many shall see, and shall fear: * and they shall hope in the Lord.

segments.t: Vidébunt multi, et timébunt: * et sperábunt in Dómino.

content.latin: 39:5 Beátus vir, cuius est nomen Dómini spes eius: * et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas.
content.english: 39:5 Blessed is the man whose trust is in the name of the Lord; * and who hath not had regard to vanities, and lying follies.

segments.t: Beátus vir, cuius est nomen Dómini spes eius: * et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas.

content.latin: 39:6 Multa fecísti tu, Dómine, Deus meus, mirabília tua: * et cogitatiónibus tuis non est qui símilis sit tibi.
content.english: 39:6 Thou hast multiplied thy wonderful works, O Lord my God: * and in thy thoughts there is no one like to thee.

segments.t: Multa fecísti tu, Dómine, Deus meus, mirabília tua: * et cogitatiónibus tuis non est qui símilis sit tibi.

content.latin: 39:6 Annuntiávi et locútus sum: * multiplicáti sunt super númerum.
content.english: 39:6 I have declared and I have spoken * they are multiplied above number.

segments.t: Annuntiávi et locútus sum: * multiplicáti sunt super númerum.

content.latin: 39:7 Sacrifícium et oblatiónem noluísti: * aures autem perfecísti mihi.
content.english: 39:7 Sacrifice and oblation thou didst not desire; * but thou hast pierced ears for me.

segments.t: Sacrifícium et oblatiónem noluísti: * aures autem perfecísti mihi.

content.latin: 39:7 Holocáustum et pro peccáto non postulásti: * tunc dixi: Ecce, vénio.
content.english: 39:7 Burnt offering and sin offering thou didst not require: * then said I, Behold I come.

segments.t: Holocáustum et pro peccáto non postulásti: * tunc dixi: Ecce, vénio.

content.latin: 39:8 In cápite libri scriptum est de me ut fácerem voluntátem tuam: * Deus meus, vólui, et legem tuam in médio cordis mei.
content.english: 39:8 In the head of the book it is written of me that I should do thy will: * O my God, I have desired it, and thy law in the midst of my heart.

segments.t: In cápite libri scriptum est de me ut fácerem voluntátem tuam: * Deus meus, vólui, et legem tuam in médio cordis mei.

content.latin: 39:10 Annuntiávi iustítiam tuam in ecclésia magna, * ecce, lábia mea non prohibébo: Dómine, tu scisti.
content.english: 39:10 I have declared thy justice in a great church, * lo, I will not restrain my lips: O Lord, thou knowest it.

segments.t: Annuntiávi iustítiam tuam in ecclésia magna, * ecce, lábia mea non prohibébo: Dómine, tu scisti.

content.latin: 39:11 Iustítiam tuam non abscóndi in corde meo: * veritátem tuam et salutáre tuum dixi.
content.english: 39:11 I have not hid thy justice within my heart: * I have declared thy truth and thy salvation.

segments.t: Iustítiam tuam non abscóndi in corde meo: * veritátem tuam et salutáre tuum dixi.

content.latin: 39:11 Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam * a concílio multo.
content.english: 39:11 I have not concealed thy mercy and thy truth * from a great council.

segments.t: Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam * a concílio multo.

content.latin: 39:12 Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me: * misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.
content.english: 39:12 Withhold not thou, O Lord, thy tender mercies from me: * thy mercy and thy truth have always upheld me.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me: * misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.

content.latin: 39:13 Quóniam circumdedérunt me mala, quorum non est númerus: * comprehendérunt me iniquitátes meæ, et non pótui ut vidérem.
content.english: 39:13 For evils without number have surrounded me; * my iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see.

segments.t: Quóniam circumdedérunt me mala, quorum non est númerus: * comprehendérunt me iniquitátes meæ, et non pótui ut vidérem.

content.latin: 39:13 Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei: * et cor meum derelíquit me.

segments.t: Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei: * et cor meum derelíquit me.

content.latin: 39:14 Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adiuvándum me réspice.
content.english: 39:14 Be pleased, O Lord to deliver me: * look down, O Lord, to help me.

segments.t: Ferant conféstim confusiónem suam, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.

content.english: 39:17 Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: * and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

segments.t: Exsúltent et læténtur super te omnes quæréntes te: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.

segments.t: Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris eius: * univérsum stratum eius versásti in infirmitáte eius.

content.latin: 40:5 Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
content.english: 40:5 I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me: * heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.

segments.t: Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.

content.latin: 40:6 Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen eius?
content.english: 40:6 My enemies have spoken evils against me: * when shall he die and his name perish?

segments.t: Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen eius?

content.latin: 40:7 Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor eius congregávit iniquitátem sibi.
content.english: 40:7 And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: * his heart gathered together iniquity to itself.

segments.t: Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor eius congregávit iniquitátem sibi.

content.latin: 40:7 Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.
content.english: 40:7 He went out * and spoke to the same purpose.

segments.t: Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.

content.latin: 40:8 Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.
content.english: 40:8 All my enemies whispered together against me: * they devised evils to me.

segments.t: Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.

content.latin: 40:9 Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
content.english: 40:9 They determined against me an unjust word: * shall he that sleepeth rise again no more?

segments.t: Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?

content.latin: 40:10 Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
content.english: 40:10 For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, * who ate my bread, hath greatly supplanted me.

segments.t: Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.

content.latin: 40:11 Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.
content.english: 40:11 But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: * and I will requite them.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.

content.latin: 40:12 In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
content.english: 40:12 By this I know, that thou hast had a good will for me: * because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.

segments.t: In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.

content.latin: 40:13 Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.
content.english: 40:13 But thou hast upheld me by reason of my innocence: * and hast established me in thy sight for ever.

segments.t: Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.

content.latin: 40:14 Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.
content.english: 40:14 Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from eternity to eternity. * So be it. So be it.

segments.t: Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Psalmus 41(2-6) [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 41(2-6)

content.latin: 41:2 Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.
content.english: 41:2 As the hart panteth after the fountains of water; * so my soul panteth after thee, O God.

segments.t: Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.

content.latin: 41:3 Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?
content.english: 41:3 My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God; * when shall I come and appear before the face of God?

segments.t: Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?

content.latin: 41:4 Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?
content.english: 41:4 My tears have been my bread day and night, * whilst it is said to me daily: Where is thy God?

segments.t: Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?

content.latin: 41:5 Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.
content.english: 41:5 These things I remembered, and poured out my soul in me: * for I shall go over into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God:

segments.t: Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.

content.latin: 41:5 In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.
content.english: 41:5 With the voice of joy and praise; * the noise of one feasting.

segments.t: In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.

content.latin: 41:6 Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?
content.english: 41:6 Why art thou sad, O my soul? * and why dost thou trouble me?

segments.t: Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?

content.latin: 41:6 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
content.english: 41:6 Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

segments.t: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
Psalmus 41(7-12)

content.latin: 41:7 Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Iordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.
content.english: 41:7 My soul is troubled within myself: * therefore will I remember thee from the land of Jordan and Hermoniim, from the little hill.

segments.t: Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Iordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.

content.latin: 41:8 Abýssus abýssum ínvocat, * in voce cataractárum tuárum.
content.english: 41:8 Deep calleth on deep, * at the noise of thy flood-gates.

segments.t: Abýssus abýssum ínvocat, * in voce cataractárum tuárum.

content.latin: 41:8 Ómnia excélsa tua, et fluctus tui * super me transiérunt.
content.english: 41:8 All thy heights and thy billows * have passed over me.

segments.t: Ómnia excélsa tua, et fluctus tui * super me transiérunt.

content.latin: 41:9 In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum eius.
content.english: 41:9 In the daytime the Lord hath commanded his mercy; * and a canticle to him in the night.

segments.t: In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum eius.

content.latin: 41:9 Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.
content.english: 41:9 With me is prayer to the God of my life. * I will say to God: Thou art my support.

segments.t: Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.

content.latin: 41:10 Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
content.english: 41:10 Why hast thou forgotten me? * and why go I mourning, whilst my enemy afflicteth me?

segments.t: Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?

content.latin: 41:11 Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.
content.english: 41:11 Whilst my bones are broken, * my enemies who trouble me have reproached me;

segments.t: Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.

content.latin: 41:11 Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?
content.english: 41:11 Whilst they say to me day by day: Where is thy God? * Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?

segments.t: Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?

content.latin: 41:12 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
content.english: 41:12 Hope thou in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

segments.t: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Suscepísti me, Dómine: et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo.
content.english: Ant. But thou hast upheld me, O Lord, and hast established me in thy sight for ever.

segments.t: Ant.
Suscepísti me, Dómine: et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo.

content.latin: Non est invéntus símilis illi, qui conserváret legem Excélsi: ídeo iureiurándo fecit illum Dóminus créscere in plebem suam.
content.english: There was not found the like to him in glory, who kept the law of the most High, and was in covenant with him. Therefore by an oath he gave him glory in his posterity, that he should increase in his people.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟.br. Elégit eum Dóminus * Sacerdótem sibi.
content.english: ℟.br. The Lord hath chosen him * for a Priest unto Himself.

segments.t: ℟.br.
Elégit eum Dóminus * Sacerdótem sibi.

content.latin: ℟. Elégit eum Dóminus * Sacerdótem sibi.
content.english: ℟. The Lord hath chosen him * for a Priest unto Himself.

segments.t: Elégit eum Dóminus * Sacerdótem sibi.

content.latin: ℣. Ad sacrificándum ei hóstiam laudis.
content.english: ℣. To offer up unto Him the sacrifice of praise.

segments.t: Ad sacrificándum ei hóstiam laudis.

content.latin: ℟. Sacerdótem sibi.
content.english: ℟. For a Priest unto Himself.

segments.t: Sacerdótem sibi.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Elégit eum Dóminus * Sacerdótem sibi.
content.english: ℟. The Lord hath chosen him * for a Priest unto Himself.

segments.t: Elégit eum Dóminus * Sacerdótem sibi.

content.latin: ℣. Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum.
content.english: ℣. Thou art a Priest for ever.

segments.t: Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum.

content.latin: ℟. Secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
content.english: ℟. After the order of Melchisedek.

segments.t: Secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, qui beátum Thomam Pontíficem insígnis in páuperes misericórdiæ virtúte decorásti: quǽsumus; ut, eius intercessióne, in omnes, qui te deprecántur, divítias misericórdiæ tuæ benígnus effúndas.
content.english: O God, Who didst adorn the blessed Bishop Thomas with the grace of an excellent pitifulness toward the needy, we entreat thee for the same thy servant's sake mercifully to pour forth the riches of thine own pitifulness upon all them which cry unto thee.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedicámus Dómino.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℣. Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

segments.t: Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

segments.t: Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.latin: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Rerum, Deus, tenax vigor,
content.english: O strength and stay upholding all creation,

content.latin: Immótus in te pérmanens,
content.english: Who ever dost thyself unmoved abide,

content.latin: Lucis diúrnæ témpora
content.english: Yet day by day the light in due gradation

content.latin: Succéssibus detérminans:
content.english: From hour to hour through all its changes guide:

content.latin: Largíre lumen véspere,
content.english: Grant to life’s day a calm unclouded ending,

content.latin: Quo vita nusquam décidat,
content.english: An eve untouched by shadows of decay,

content.latin: Sed prǽmium mortis sacræ
content.english: The brightness of a holy death-bed blending

content.latin: Perénnis instet glória.
content.english: With dawning glories of th’ eternal day.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: Hear us, O Father, gracious and forgiving,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: And thou, O Christ, the co-eternal Word,

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost, by all things living

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Now and to endless ages art adored.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Salvásti nos, * Dómine, et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽcula.
content.english: Ant. Thou hast saved us, O Lord, * and in thy name we will give praise for ever.

segments.t: Ant.
Salvásti nos, * Dómine, et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽcula.

content.latin: Psalmus 43(2-9) [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 43(2-9)

content.latin: 43:2 Deus áuribus nostris audívimus: * patres nostri annuntiavérunt nobis.
content.english: 43:2 We have heard, O God, with our ears: * our fathers have declared to us,

segments.t: Deus áuribus nostris audívimus: * patres nostri annuntiavérunt nobis.

content.latin: 43:2 Opus, quod operátus es in diébus eórum, * et in diébus antíquis.
content.english: 43:2 The work thou hast wrought in their days, * and in the days of old.

segments.t: Opus, quod operátus es in diébus eórum, * et in diébus antíquis.

content.latin: 43:3 Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos: * afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.
content.english: 43:3 Thy hand destroyed the Gentiles, and thou plantedst them: * thou didst afflict the people and cast them out.

segments.t: Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos: * afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.

content.latin: 43:4 Nec enim in gládio suo possedérunt terram, * et brácchium eórum non salvávit eos:
content.english: 43:4 For they got not the possession of the land by their own sword: * neither did their own arm save them.

segments.t: Nec enim in gládio suo possedérunt terram, * et brácchium eórum non salvávit eos:

content.latin: 43:4 Sed déxtera tua, et brácchium tuum, et illuminátio vultus tui: * quóniam complacuísti in eis.
content.english: 43:4 But thy right hand and thy arm, and the light of thy countenance: * because thou wast pleased with them.

segments.t: Sed déxtera tua, et brácchium tuum, et illuminátio vultus tui: * quóniam complacuísti in eis.

content.latin: 43:5 Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus: * qui mandas salútes Iacob.
content.english: 43:5 Thou art thyself my king and my God, * who commandest the saving of Jacob.

segments.t: Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus: * qui mandas salútes Iacob.

content.latin: 43:6 In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu: * et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.
content.english: 43:6 Through thee we will push down our enemies with the horn: * and through thy name we will despise them that rise up against us.

segments.t: In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu: * et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.

content.latin: 43:7 Non enim in arcu meo sperábo: * et gládius meus non salvábit me.
content.english: 43:7 For I will not trust in my bow: * neither shall my sword save me.

segments.t: Non enim in arcu meo sperábo: * et gládius meus non salvábit me.

content.latin: 43:8 Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos: * et odiéntes nos confudísti.
content.english: 43:8 But thou hast saved us from them that afflict us: * and hast put them to shame that hate us.

segments.t: Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos: * et odiéntes nos confudísti.

content.latin: 43:9 In Deo laudábimur tota die: * et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽculum.
content.english: 43:9 In God shall we glory all the day long: * and in thy name we will give praise for ever.

segments.t: In Deo laudábimur tota die: * et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽculum.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
Psalmus 43(10-20)

content.latin: 43:10 Nunc autem repulísti et confudísti nos: * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris.
content.english: 43:10 But now thou hast cast us off, and put us to shame: * and thou, O God, wilt not go out with our armies.

segments.t: Nunc autem repulísti et confudísti nos: * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris.

content.latin: 43:11 Avertísti nos retrórsum post inimícos nostros: * et qui odérunt nos, diripiébant sibi.
content.english: 43:11 Thou hast made us turn our back to our enemies: * and they that hated us plundered for themselves.

segments.t: Avertísti nos retrórsum post inimícos nostros: * et qui odérunt nos, diripiébant sibi.

content.latin: 43:12 Dedísti nos tamquam oves escárum: * et in géntibus dispersísti nos.
content.english: 43:12 Thou hast given us up like sheep to be eaten: * thou hast scattered us among the nations.

segments.t: Dedísti nos tamquam oves escárum: * et in géntibus dispersísti nos.

content.latin: 43:13 Vendidísti pópulum tuum sine prétio: * et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum.
content.english: 43:13 Thou hast sold thy people for no price: * and there was no reckoning in the exchange of them.

segments.t: Vendidísti pópulum tuum sine prétio: * et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum.

content.latin: 43:14 Posuísti nos oppróbrium vicínis nostris, * subsannatiónem et derísum his, qui sunt in circúitu nostro.
content.english: 43:14 Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours, * a scoff and derision to them that are round about us.

segments.t: Posuísti nos oppróbrium vicínis nostris, * subsannatiónem et derísum his, qui sunt in circúitu nostro.

content.latin: 43:15 Posuísti nos in similitúdinem géntibus: * commotiónem cápitis in pópulis.
content.english: 43:15 Thou hast made us a byword among the Gentiles: * a shaking of the head among the people.

segments.t: Posuísti nos in similitúdinem géntibus: * commotiónem cápitis in pópulis.

content.latin: 43:16 Tota die verecúndia mea contra me est, * et confúsio faciéi meæ coopéruit me.
content.english: 43:16 All the day long my shame is before me: * and the confusion of my face hath covered me.

segments.t: Tota die verecúndia mea contra me est, * et confúsio faciéi meæ coopéruit me.

content.latin: 43:17 A voce exprobrántis, et obloquéntis: * a fácie inimíci, et persequéntis.
content.english: 43:17 At the voice of him that reproacheth and detracteth me: * at the face of the enemy and persecutor.

segments.t: A voce exprobrántis, et obloquéntis: * a fácie inimíci, et persequéntis.

content.latin: 43:18 Hæc ómnia venérunt super nos, nec oblíti sumus te: * et iníque non égimus in testaménto tuo.
content.english: 43:18 All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten thee: * and we have not done wickedly in thy covenant.

segments.t: Hæc ómnia venérunt super nos, nec oblíti sumus te: * et iníque non égimus in testaménto tuo.

content.latin: 43:19 Et non recéssit retro cor nostrum: * et declinásti sémitas nostras a via tua:
content.english: 43:19 And our heart hath not turned back: * neither hast thou turned aside our steps from thy way.

segments.t: Et non recéssit retro cor nostrum: * et declinásti sémitas nostras a via tua:

content.latin: 43:20 Quóniam humiliásti nos in loco afflictiónis, * et coopéruit nos umbra mortis.
content.english: 43:20 For thou hast humbled us in the place of affliction: * and the shadow of death hath covered us.

segments.t: Quóniam humiliásti nos in loco afflictiónis, * et coopéruit nos umbra mortis.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Psalmus 43(21-26)

content.latin: 43:21 Si oblíti sumus nomen Dei nostri, * et si expándimus manus nostras ad deum aliénum:
content.english: 43:21 If we have forgotten the name of our God, * and if we have spread forth our hands to a strange god:

segments.t: Si oblíti sumus nomen Dei nostri, * et si expándimus manus nostras ad deum aliénum:

content.latin: 43:22 Nonne Deus requíret ista? * ipse enim novit abscóndita cordis.
content.english: 43:22 Shall not God search out these things: * for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.

segments.t: Nonne Deus requíret ista? * ipse enim novit abscóndita cordis.

content.latin: 43:22 Quóniam propter te mortificámur tota die: * æstimáti sumus sicut oves occisiónis.
content.english: 43:22 Because for thy sake we are killed all the day long: * we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.

segments.t: Quóniam propter te mortificámur tota die: * æstimáti sumus sicut oves occisiónis.

content.latin: 43:23 Exsúrge, quare obdórmis, Dómine? * exsúrge, et ne repéllas in finem.
content.english: 43:23 Arise, why sleepest thou, O Lord? * arise, and cast us not off to the end.

segments.t: Exsúrge, quare obdórmis, Dómine? * exsúrge, et ne repéllas in finem.

content.latin: 43:24 Quare fáciem tuam avértis, * oblivísceris inópiæ nostræ, et tribulatiónis nostræ?
content.english: 43:24 Why turnest thou thy face away? * and forgettest our want and our trouble?

segments.t: Quare fáciem tuam avértis, * oblivísceris inópiæ nostræ, et tribulatiónis nostræ?

content.latin: 43:25 Quóniam humiliáta est in púlvere ánima nostra: * conglutinátus est in terra venter noster.
content.english: 43:25 For our soul is humbled down to the dust: * our belly cleaveth to the earth.

segments.t: Quóniam humiliáta est in púlvere ánima nostra: * conglutinátus est in terra venter noster.

content.latin: 43:26 Exsúrge, Dómine, ádiuva nos: * et rédime nos propter nomen tuum.
content.english: 43:26 Arise, O Lord, help us * and redeem us for thy name’s sake.

segments.t: Exsúrge, Dómine, ádiuva nos: * et rédime nos propter nomen tuum.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, qui beátum Thomam Pontíficem insígnis in páuperes misericórdiæ virtúte decorásti: quǽsumus; ut, eius intercessióne, in omnes, qui te deprecántur, divítias misericórdiæ tuæ benígnus effúndas.
content.english: O God, Who didst adorn the blessed Bishop Thomas with the grace of an excellent pitifulness toward the needy, we entreat thee for the same thy servant's sake mercifully to pour forth the riches of thine own pitifulness upon all them which cry unto thee.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: Psalm 122 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 122

content.latin: 122:1 Ad te levávi óculos meos, * qui hábitas in cælis.
content.english: 122:1 To thee have I lifted up my eyes, * who dwellest in heaven.

segments.t: Ad te levávi óculos meos, * qui hábitas in cælis.

content.latin: 122:2 Ecce, sicut óculi servórum * in mánibus dominórum suórum,
content.english: 122:2 Behold as the eyes of servants * are on the hands of their masters,

segments.t: Ecce, sicut óculi servórum * in mánibus dominórum suórum,

content.latin: 122:2 Sicut óculi ancíllæ in mánibus dóminæ suæ: * ita óculi nostri ad Dóminum, Deum nostrum, donec misereátur nostri.
content.english: 122:2 As the eyes of the handmaid are on the hands of her mistress: * so are our eyes unto the Lord our God, until he have mercy on us.

segments.t: Sicut óculi ancíllæ in mánibus dóminæ suæ: * ita óculi nostri ad Dóminum, Deum nostrum, donec misereátur nostri.

content.latin: 122:3 Miserére nostri, Dómine, miserére nostri: * quia multum repléti sumus despectióne:
content.english: 122:3 Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: * for we are greatly filled with contempt.

segments.t: Miserére nostri, Dómine, miserére nostri: * quia multum repléti sumus despectióne:

content.latin: 122:4 Quia multum repléta est ánima nostra: * oppróbrium abundántibus, et despéctio supérbis.
content.english: 122:4 For our soul is greatly filled: * we are a reproach to the rich, and contempt to the proud.

segments.t: Quia multum repléta est ánima nostra: * oppróbrium abundántibus, et despéctio supérbis.

content.english: Psalm 123 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 123

content.latin: 123:1 Nisi quia Dóminus erat in nobis, dicat nunc Israël: * nisi quia Dóminus erat in nobis,
content.english: 123:1 If it had not been that the Lord was with us, let Israel now say: * If it had not been that the Lord was with us,

segments.t: Nisi quia Dóminus erat in nobis, dicat nunc Israël: * nisi quia Dóminus erat in nobis,

content.latin: 123:2 Cum exsúrgerent hómines in nos, * forte vivos deglutíssent nos:
content.english: 123:2 When men rose up against us, * perhaps they had swallowed us up alive.

segments.t: Cum exsúrgerent hómines in nos, * forte vivos deglutíssent nos:

content.latin: 123:3 Cum irascerétur furor eórum in nos, * fórsitan aqua absorbuísset nos.
content.english: 123:3 When their fury was enkindled against us, * perhaps the waters had swallowed us up.

segments.t: Cum irascerétur furor eórum in nos, * fórsitan aqua absorbuísset nos.

content.latin: 123:5 Torréntem pertransívit ánima nostra: * fórsitan pertransísset ánima nostra aquam intolerábilem.
content.english: 123:5 Our soul hath passed through a torrent: * perhaps our soul had passed through a water insupportable.

segments.t: Torréntem pertransívit ánima nostra: * fórsitan pertransísset ánima nostra aquam intolerábilem.

content.latin: 123:6 Benedíctus Dóminus * qui non dedit nos in captiónem déntibus eórum.
content.english: 123:6 Blessed be the Lord, * who hath not given us to be a prey to their teeth.

segments.t: Benedíctus Dóminus * qui non dedit nos in captiónem déntibus eórum.

content.latin: 123:7 Ánima nostra sicut passer erépta est * de láqueo venántium:
content.english: 123:7 Our soul hath been delivered as a sparrow * out of the snare of the fowlers.

segments.t: Ánima nostra sicut passer erépta est * de láqueo venántium:

content.latin: 123:7 Láqueus contrítus est, * et nos liberáti sumus.
content.english: 123:7 The snare is broken, * and we are delivered.

segments.t: Láqueus contrítus est, * et nos liberáti sumus.

content.latin: 123:8 Adiutórium nostrum in nómine Dómini, * qui fecit cælum et terram.
content.english: 123:8 Our help is in the name of the Lord, * who made heaven and earth.

segments.t: Adiutórium nostrum in nómine Dómini, * qui fecit cælum et terram.

segments.t: Psalmus 124

content.latin: 124:1 Qui confídunt in Dómino, sicut mons Sion: * non commovébitur in ætérnum, qui hábitat in Ierúsalem.
content.english: 124:1 They that trust in the Lord shall be as mount Sion: * he shall not be moved for ever that dwelleth in Jerusalem.

segments.t: Qui confídunt in Dómino, sicut mons Sion: * non commovébitur in ætérnum, qui hábitat in Ierúsalem.

content.latin: 124:2 Montes in circúitu eius: * et Dóminus in circúitu pópuli sui, ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum.
content.english: 124:2 Mountains are round about it: * so the Lord is round about his people from henceforth now and for ever.

segments.t: Montes in circúitu eius: * et Dóminus in circúitu pópuli sui, ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum.

content.latin: 124:3 Quia non relínquet Dóminus virgam peccatórum super sortem iustórum: * ut non exténdant iusti ad iniquitátem manus suas.
content.english: 124:3 For the Lord will not leave the rod of sinners upon the lot of the just: * that the just may not stretch forth their hands to iniquity.

segments.t: Quia non relínquet Dóminus virgam peccatórum super sortem iustórum: * ut non exténdant iusti ad iniquitátem manus suas.

content.latin: 124:4 Bénefac, Dómine, bonis, * et rectis corde.
content.english: 124:4 Do good, O Lord, to those that are good, * and to the upright of heart.

segments.t: Bénefac, Dómine, bonis, * et rectis corde.

content.latin: 124:5 Declinántes autem in obligatiónes addúcet Dóminus cum operántibus iniquitátem: * pax super Israël.
content.english: 124:5 But such as turn aside into bonds, the Lord shall lead out with the workers of iniquity: * peace upon Israel.

segments.t: Declinántes autem in obligatiónes addúcet Dóminus cum operántibus iniquitátem: * pax super Israël.

Magnificávit Dóminus * fácere nobíscum: facti sumus lætántes.

content.english: Psalm 125 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 125

content.latin: 125:1 In converténdo Dóminus captivitátem Sion: * facti sumus sicut consoláti:
content.english: 125:1 When the Lord brought back the captivity of Sion, * we became like men comforted.

segments.t: In converténdo Dóminus captivitátem Sion: * facti sumus sicut consoláti:

content.latin: 125:2 Tunc replétum est gáudio os nostrum: * et lingua nostra exsultatióne.
content.english: 125:2 Then was our mouth filled with gladness; * and our tongue with joy.

segments.t: Tunc replétum est gáudio os nostrum: * et lingua nostra exsultatióne.

content.latin: 125:2 Tunc dicent inter gentes: * Magnificávit Dóminus fácere cum eis.
content.english: 125:2 Then shall they say among the Gentiles: * The Lord hath done great things for them.

segments.t: Tunc dicent inter gentes: * Magnificávit Dóminus fácere cum eis.

content.latin: 125:3 Magnificávit Dóminus fácere nobíscum: * facti sumus lætántes.
content.english: 125:3 The Lord hath done great things for us: * we are become joyful.

segments.t: Magnificávit Dóminus fácere nobíscum: * facti sumus lætántes.

content.latin: 125:4 Convérte, Dómine, captivitátem nostram, * sicut torrens in Austro.
content.english: 125:4 Turn again our captivity, O Lord, * as a stream in the south.

segments.t: Convérte, Dómine, captivitátem nostram, * sicut torrens in Austro.

content.latin: 125:5 Qui séminant in lácrimis, * in exsultatióne metent.
content.english: 125:5 They that sow in tears * shall reap in joy.

segments.t: Qui séminant in lácrimis, * in exsultatióne metent.

content.latin: 125:6 Eúntes ibant et flebant, * mitténtes sémina sua.
content.english: 125:6 Going they went and wept, * casting their seeds.

segments.t: Eúntes ibant et flebant, * mitténtes sémina sua.

content.latin: 125:6 Veniéntes autem vénient cum exsultatióne, * portántes manípulos suos.
content.english: 125:6 But coming they shall come with joyfulness, * carrying their sheaves.

segments.t: Veniéntes autem vénient cum exsultatióne, * portántes manípulos suos.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris: et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem: sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation: But deliver us from evil. Amen.

content.latin: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Ioánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, et ómnibus Sanctis, quia peccávi nimis, cogitatióne, verbo et ópere: percutit sibi pectus mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa. Ídeo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum, beátum Ioánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, et omnes Sanctos, oráre pro me ad Dóminum Deum nostrum.
content.english: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and to all the Saints, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed: strikes his breast through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the Saints, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

segments.t: Úsquequo, Dómine, obliviscéris me in finem? * Úsquequo avértis fáciem tuam a me?

content.latin: 12:2 Quámdiu ponam consília in ánima mea, * dolórem in corde meo per diem?
content.english: 12:2 How long shall I take counsels in my soul, * sorrow in my heart all the day?

segments.t: Quámdiu ponam consília in ánima mea, * dolórem in corde meo per diem?

content.latin: 12:3 Úsquequo exaltábitur inimícus meus super me? * réspice, et exáudi me, Dómine, Deus meus.
content.english: 12:3 How long shall my enemy be exalted over me? * Consider, and hear me, O Lord my God.

segments.t: Úsquequo exaltábitur inimícus meus super me? * réspice, et exáudi me, Dómine, Deus meus.

content.latin: 12:4 Illúmina óculos meos ne umquam obdórmiam in morte: * nequándo dicat inimícus meus: Præválui advérsus eum.
content.english: 12:4 Enlighten my eyes that I never sleep in death: * lest at any time my enemy say: I have prevailed against him.

segments.t: Illúmina óculos meos ne umquam obdórmiam in morte: * nequándo dicat inimícus meus: Præválui advérsus eum.

content.latin: 12:5 Qui tríbulant me, exsultábunt si motus fúero: * ego autem in misericórdia tua sperávi.
content.english: 12:5 They that trouble me will rejoice when I am moved: * but I have trusted in thy mercy.

segments.t: Qui tríbulant me, exsultábunt si motus fúero: * ego autem in misericórdia tua sperávi.

content.latin: 12:6 Exsultábit cor meum in salutári tuo: cantábo Dómino qui bona tríbuit mihi: * et psallam nómini Dómini altíssimi.
content.english: 12:6 My heart shall rejoice in thy salvation: I will sing to the Lord, who giveth me good things: * yea, I will sing to the name of the Lord the most High.

segments.t: Exsultábit cor meum in salutári tuo: cantábo Dómino qui bona tríbuit mihi: * et psallam nómini Dómini altíssimi.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Psalmus 15 [3]
content.english: Psalm 15 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 15

content.latin: 15:1 Consérva me, Dómine, quóniam sperávi in te. * Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu, quóniam bonórum meórum non eges.
content.english: 15:1 Preserve me, O Lord, for I have put my trust in thee. * I have said to the Lord, thou art my God, for thou hast no need of my goods.

segments.t: Consérva me, Dómine, quóniam sperávi in te. * Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu, quóniam bonórum meórum non eges.

content.latin: 15:3 Sanctis, qui sunt in terra eius, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas in eis.
content.english: 15:3 To the saints, who are in his land, * he hath made wonderful all my desires in them.

segments.t: Sanctis, qui sunt in terra eius, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas in eis.

content.latin: 15:4 Multiplicátæ sunt infirmitátes eórum: * póstea acceleravérunt.
content.english: 15:4 Their infirmities were multiplied: * afterwards they made haste.

segments.t: Multiplicátæ sunt infirmitátes eórum: * póstea acceleravérunt.

content.latin: 15:4 Non congregábo conventícula eórum de sanguínibus, * nec memor ero nóminum eórum per lábia mea.
content.english: 15:4 I will not gather together their meetings for blood offerings: * nor will I be mindful of their names by my lips.

segments.t: Non congregábo conventícula eórum de sanguínibus, * nec memor ero nóminum eórum per lábia mea.

content.latin: 15:5 Dóminus pars hereditátis meæ, et cálicis mei: * tu es, qui restítues hereditátem meam mihi.
content.english: 15:5 The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup: * it is thou that wilt restore my inheritance to me.

segments.t: Dóminus pars hereditátis meæ, et cálicis mei: * tu es, qui restítues hereditátem meam mihi.

content.latin: 15:6 Funes cecidérunt mihi in præcláris: * étenim heréditas mea præclára est mihi.
content.english: 15:6 The lines are fallen unto me in goodly places: * for my inheritance is goodly to me.

segments.t: Funes cecidérunt mihi in præcláris: * étenim heréditas mea præclára est mihi.

content.latin: 15:7 Benedícam Dóminum, qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum: * ínsuper et usque ad noctem increpuérunt me renes mei.
content.english: 15:7 I will bless the Lord, who hath given me understanding: * moreover my reins also have corrected me even till night.

segments.t: Benedícam Dóminum, qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum: * ínsuper et usque ad noctem increpuérunt me renes mei.

content.latin: 15:8 Providébam Dóminum in conspéctu meo semper: * quóniam a dextris est mihi, ne commóvear.
content.english: 15:8 I set the Lord always in my sight: * for he is at my right hand, that I be not moved.

segments.t: Providébam Dóminum in conspéctu meo semper: * quóniam a dextris est mihi, ne commóvear.

content.latin: 15:9 Propter hoc lætátum est cor meum, et exsultávit lingua mea: * ínsuper et caro mea requiéscet in spe.
content.english: 15:9 Therefore my heart hath been glad, and my tongue hath rejoiced: * moreover my flesh also shall rest in hope.

segments.t: Propter hoc lætátum est cor meum, et exsultávit lingua mea: * ínsuper et caro mea requiéscet in spe.

content.latin: 15:10 Quóniam non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno: * nec dabis sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem.
content.english: 15:10 Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; * nor wilt thou give thy holy one to see corruption.

segments.t: Quóniam non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno: * nec dabis sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem.

content.latin: 15:11 Notas mihi fecísti vias vitæ, adimplébis me lætítia cum vultu tuo: * delectatiónes in déxtera tua usque in finem.
content.english: 15:11 Thou hast made known to me the ways of life, thou shalt fill me with joy with thy countenance: * at thy right hand are delights even to the end.

segments.t: Notas mihi fecísti vias vitæ, adimplébis me lætítia cum vultu tuo: * delectatiónes in déxtera tua usque in finem.

content.latin: Ant. Tu, Dómine, servábis nos: et custódies nos in ætérnum.
content.english: Ant. Thou, O Lord, wilt preserve us: and keep us for ever.

segments.t: Ant.
Tu, Dómine, servábis nos: et custódies nos in ætérnum.

content.latin: Te lucis ante términum,
content.english: Before the ending of the day,

content.latin: Rerum Creátor, póscimus,
content.english: Creator of the world, we pray

content.latin: Ut pro tua cleméntia
content.english: That with thy wonted favor thou

content.latin: Sis præsul et custódia.
content.english: Wouldst be our guard and keeper now.

content.latin: Procul recédant sómnia,
content.english: From all ill dreams defend our eyes,

content.latin: Et nóctium phantásmata;
content.english: From nightly fears and fantasies;

content.latin: Hostémque nostrum cómprime,
content.english: Tread under foot our ghostly foe,

content.latin: Ne polluántur córpora.
content.english: That no pollution we may know.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: O Father, that we ask be done,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thine only Son;

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Doth live and reign eternally.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.english: Jer 14:9

segments.t: Ier 14:9

content.latin: Tu autem in nobis es, Dómine, et nomen sanctum tuum invocátum est super nos: ne derelínquas nos, Dómine, Deus noster.
content.english: But thou, O Lord, art among us, and thy name is called upon by us: forsake us not, O Lord our God.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℣. Custódi nos, Dómine, ut pupíllam óculi.
content.english: ℣. Keep us, Lord, as the apple of thine eye.

segments.t: Custódi nos, Dómine, ut pupíllam óculi.

content.latin: ℟. Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege nos.
content.english: ℟. Protect us under the shadow of thy wings.

segments.t: Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege nos.

content.english: Ant. Protect us, * Lord, while we are awake and safeguard us while we sleep; that we may keep watch with Christ, and rest in peace.

Salva nos, * Dómine, vigilántes, custódi nos dormiéntes; ut vigilémus cum Christo, et requiescámus in pace.

content.latin: 2:29 Nunc dimíttis ✠ servum tuum, Dómine, * secúndum verbum tuum in pace:
content.english: 2:29 Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, ✠ * according to thy word in peace;

segments.t: Nunc dimíttis ✠ servum tuum, Dómine, * secúndum verbum tuum in pace:

content.latin: 2:30 Quia vidérunt óculi mei * salutáre tuum,
content.english: 2:30 Because my eyes have seen * thy salvation,

segments.t: Quia vidérunt óculi mei * salutáre tuum,

content.latin: 2:31 Quod parásti * ante fáciem ómnium populórum,
content.english: 2:31 Which thou hast prepared * before the face of all peoples:

segments.t: Quod parásti * ante fáciem ómnium populórum,

content.latin: 2:32 Lumen ad revelatiónem géntium, * et glóriam plebis tuæ Israël.
content.english: 2:32 A light to the revelation of the Gentiles, * and the glory of thy people Israel.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Vísita, quǽsumus, Dómine, habitatiónem istam, et omnes insídias inimíci ab ea longe repélle: Ángeli tui sancti hábitent in ea, qui nos in pace custódiant; et benedíctio tua sit super nos semper.
content.english: Visit, we beseech thee, O Lord, this dwelling, and drive far from it the snares of the enemy; let thy holy angels dwell herein to preserve us in peace, and let thy blessing be always upon us.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedícat et custódiat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus, ✠ Pater, et Fílius, et Spíritus Sanctus.
content.english: Benediction. The almighty and merciful Lord, ✠ the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, bless us and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Benedícat et custódiat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus, ✠ Pater, et Fílius, et Spíritus Sanctus.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Salve, Regína, mater misericórdiæ;
content.english: Hail holy Queen, Mother of Mercy,

content.latin: vita, dulcédo et spes nóstra, salve.
content.english: our life, our sweetness, and our hope.

content.latin: Ad te clamámus éxsules fílii Hevæ.
content.english: To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve.

content.latin: Ad te suspirámus geméntes et flentes
content.english: To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping

content.latin: In hac lacrimárum valle.
content.english: In this valley of tears.

content.latin: Eia ergo, advocáta nostra,
content.english: Turn then, most gracious Advocate,

content.latin: illos tuos misericórdes óculos ad nos convérte.
content.english: thine eyes of mercy toward us.

content.latin: Et Iesum, benedíctum fructum ventris tui,
content.english: And after this our exile show unto us

content.latin: nobis post hoc exsílium osténde.
content.english: the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

content.latin: O clemens, o pia, o dulcis Virgo María.
content.english: O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

content.latin: ℣. Ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génetrix.
content.english: ℣. Pray for us, O Holy Mother of God.

segments.t: Ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génetrix.

content.latin: ℟. Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.
content.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

segments.t: Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui gloriósæ Vírginis Matris Maríæ corpus et ánimam, ut dignum Fílii tui habitáculum éffici mererétur, Spíritu Sancto cooperánte, præparásti: da, ut, cuius commemoratióne lætámur, eius pia intercessióne, ab instántibus malis et a morte perpétua liberémur. Per eúndem Christum Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
content.english: O almighty, everlasting God, who by the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, didst prepare the body and soul of Mary, glorious Virgin and Mother, to become a worthy dwelling for Thy Son; grant that we who rejoice in her commemoration may, by her gracious intercession, be delivered from present evils and from everlasting death. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.
content.english: ℣. May the divine assistance ✠ remain with us always.

segments.t: Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.
